issue.title: Highlights URL validation accepts IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals for private hosts

task_type_fields.impact: `validate_and_clean` gates every URL that `bob highlights clip` and `bob highlights create` capture. It also checks every redirect hop that the new curl fetcher (`fetch.rs`, epic bob-cli-4s) follows. The private-host rule is a documented contract ("public http(s) only, no userinfo, no private hosts"). An IPv4-mapped literal bypasses it, either typed directly or returned in a redirect `Location`, so bob can be pointed at loopback or LAN/Tailnet services. Exposure is low because Bryan chooses the URLs, but the contract is silently wrong.
task_type_fields.repro:
Build bob from master fe1c05f. Use a scratch vault and a curl stub that always fails, so nothing is fetched:

    V=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $V/lib $V/ref $V/xlib
    BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_CURL=/bin/false bob highlights create 'http://127.0.0.1/x.pdf' -d -b $V
    #  -> error: private IP literal is not captured: "127.0.0.1"   (correct)
    BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_CURL=/bin/false bob highlights create 'http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/x.pdf' -d -b $V
    #  -> error: curl failed (exit 1) for http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/x.pdf   (validation passed; curl was invoked)
    BOB_HIGHLIGHTS_CURL=/bin/false bob highlights create 'http://[::ffff:10.0.0.1]/x.pdf' -d -b $V
    #  -> error: curl failed (exit 1) for http://[::ffff:a00:1]/x.pdf

Root cause: `is_non_global_literal` in `src/native/highlights_ref/clip_url.rs` (introduced in 44bfe589) checks IPv6 literals with `is_loopback`, `is_unspecified`, link-local and unique-local only. Rust's `Ipv6Addr::is_loopback` matches only `::1`, so an IPv4-mapped literal (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) that embeds a loopback, RFC 1918, link-local or CGNAT/Tailscale IPv4 address passes. The fix is to map the address with `Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4_mapped()` (and consider the deprecated IPv4-compatible `::a.b.c.d` form and NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`), apply the IPv4 rules to the embedded address, and add `validate_and_clean` unit tests for each form.

Separate design gap, out of scope for this fix: only the hostname string is checked, so a public DNS name that resolves to a private address is not blocked. Pinning the resolved address (for example curl `--resolve`) would also have to cover the clip adapter's browser navigation.

issue.creation_reason: The bob-cli-4s land audit found that the private-host check, which now also guards every curl redirect hop that create follows, misses IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals. The defect predates that epic (44bfe589), so it is filed separately instead of being folded into the epic's remaining work.
